Poll
pōl
n. and v. (the head; hence to number by heads, and to cut the hair of the head)
From an old Germanic word for the head or top — the same root that gives polled cattle and, much later, a poll of voters counted by heads. In the Authorized Version the word means the head itself, and both its senses follow from that.

Biblical Definition

The old English poll is the head, and Scripture uses it in both directions. Counted: “Thou shalt even take five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary shalt thou take them” (Num 3:47) — the redemption money for the firstborn of Israel who exceeded the number of the Levites, five shekels a head. A census in Israel is a counting of heads for a redemption price, which is why David's numbering without the ransom brought a plague. Cut: the priests of Ezekiel's temple “shall not shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads” (Eze 44:20) — neither the shaven head of pagan mourning nor the long unbound hair of the Nazarite, but trimmed. The priesthood was to look like neither the mourner nor the ascetic; a settled, ordinary appearance was itself a testimony. And Micah, ordering a nation into mourning: “Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee” (Mic 1:16). The delicate children — the ones raised carefully, in comfort — are the ones carried away, and the prophet tells the mothers to cut off their hair.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines poll as the head of a person, and hence a register of heads or persons; and as a verb, to lop the tops of trees or to cut off the hair of the head.

expand to see more

POLL, n. The head of a person, or the back part of the head.

1. A register of heads, that is, of persons; as, to take the poll.

2. An election, or the place where an election is held; so called from the counting of heads.

POLL, v.t. To lop the tops of trees; to clip; to shear; as, to poll the head.

1. To enter or register the names of persons.

Key Scripture

Num 3:47 — "Thou shalt even take five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary shalt thou take them: (the shekel is twenty gerahs:)"

Eze 44:20 — "Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads."

Mic 1:16 — "Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee."

Modern Corruption

Ministers are shaped by the extremes of the surrounding culture; Ezekiel forbids the priests both the shaven head and the flowing locks.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 44:20 is a small verse with a durable application. The priest was to look like neither of the two available religious types: not the shaven head of the pagan mourning rites Israel was forbidden to copy, and not the long unbound hair that marked the Nazarite's temporary separation. He was to be trimmed — ordinary, kept, unremarkable. The temptation for those who serve God has always been to signal by appearance, whether by adopting the surrounding culture's markers or by adopting a conspicuous holiness that advertises itself. The ceremonial detail is fulfilled and no longer binds; the instinct behind it — that a minister's appearance should draw no attention to itself in either direction — has not aged.

Micah supplies the other application, and it is severe. Poll thee for thy delicate children — the children reared in comfort and carefully spared every hardship are the ones described going into captivity. A generation raised for softness has no defence when the Assyrian comes. Scripture's alternative is not harshness toward children, which it forbids, but the deliberate formation of them in the fear of the LORD — teaching them diligently, sitting, walking, lying down and rising up — so that they are ready for a world that will not be delicate with them.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew gulgoleth (H1538), a skull, a head — and the root of Golgotha; kasam (H3697), to trim or shear; qarach (H7139), to make bald.

expand to see more

Hebrew gulgoleth (H1538) — a skull, a head, a poll; Numbers 3:47, Exodus 38:26 — and the Aramaic form gives Golgotha, the place of a skull.

Hebrew kasam (H3697) — to shear, to trim; Ezekiel 44:20, they shall only poll their heads — its only occurrence.

Hebrew qarach (H7139) — to make bald; Micah 1:16, a sign of mourning forbidden to priests but commanded here to a nation.

Hebrew pidyom (H6306) — a ransom, redemption money; the five shekels a head for the firstborn.

Hebrew 'anugim (H8588) — delicate, dainty, tenderly reared; Micah 1:16, the children carried away.

Usage

"“Five shekels apiece by the poll” — redemption money, head by head."

"“They shall only poll their heads” — neither shaven nor flowing."

"“Poll thee for thy delicate children” — and they were the ones taken."
